methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops led by a Norfolk native directly target capability distribution through peer learning networks, creating grassroots AI fluency outside traditional tech hubs—a prototype for distributed deep adoption if it scales beyond individual initiative.

signals.title: How one Virginia county’s AI platform protects sensitive data - Route Fifty
signals.signal_reading: A Virginia county building its own AI platform with data sovereignty demonstrates institutional capacity for deep, self-directed AI implementation beyond commercial platforms—signaling potential for distributed technical capability if knowledge transfers across jurisdictions.

signals.title: Veterans with vision loss find new ‘eyes’ through AI glasses
signals.signal_reading: Meta Ray-Bans delivering AI assistance to veterans in historically underserved regions shows shallow but democratizing platform adoption—though device distribution without local technical capacity building risks widening the depth gap even as access spreads.

signals.title: Virginia Tech sets course for human-centered AI leadership - Virginia Tech News
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech's human-centered AI leadership initiative positions a non-NoVA institution as a knowledge distribution hub, creating potential pathways for deep capability to radiate through education networks across rural and underserved regions statewide.

signals.title: Roanoke College joins Google AI for Education Accelerator - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College joining Google's AI Education Accelerator represents platform-mediated adoption in a smaller market—Google provides tools but controls depth, creating risk of shallow implementation unless faculty develop independent technical capacity beyond the provided curriculum.
